events.name: Founders Friday w/ Constrafor
events.description: Join us Friday (3/21) for an exclusive fireside chat with Anwar Ghauche, Founder & CEO of Constrafor. Constrafor is a construction-oriented fintech & SaaS startup, building a procurement platform with embedded financing. Simply put: they automate critical back-office tasks for general contractors & offers subcontractors with innovative financing solutions like Early Pay, helping improve cash flow & enabling business growth. Anwar uniquely combines expertise in civil engineering, finance, & AI. His journey includes roles at QVT Financial & leading AI strategy at SparkCognition, backed by an MBA from Stanford & a Master's in Civil Engineering from MIT. We'll discuss Anwar's founder journey, the complexities of building software for a very physical industry, & the role of fintech in changing how construction & contractors can work. This event is open-invite. events.name: [Open Data Week] Bodies Of Data Exhibition Opening Reception
events.description: Event Info is pleased to announce the opening of Corpus: Bodies of Data, a public exhibition of ten data-driven, interdisciplinary art projects presented in partnership with BRIC. We invite you to join us for the opening reception on Friday, March 21 from 6:30 - 8:30 pm.  Please RSVP for a (free) ticket. About the Exhibition: Corpus: Bodies of Data is the 2025 exhibition of , an annual data art exhibition featuring works that creatively analyze, interpret, & interrogate data made available in NYC's Open Data Portal. This exhibition is presented by DxD in partnership with BRIC & is on display at BRIC House from March 22 through April 6, 2025, from 12pm - 7pm daily.  Corpus carries multiple meanings. A corpus might be a body of work, knowledge, literature, or language - the embodiment of activity, values, or beliefs. Corpus can also mean a physical body, an aggregation of organisms, a group of elements or people, or the corporeal substance of a thing.   This year, DxD asked artists to think about the concept of a corpus, or body of data, that can be physical or ephemeral. We imagine a dataset as a body of knowledge that indexes people in a community, events in a timeline, or observations in an area. But datasets are also representations of our bodies & the corpora of living things; collections of individuals, bodies of water, natural & human-made systems, the collectivity of the city. How are these bodies of knowledge born, how do they age, grow, & go through cycles - who animates them & do they expire? And, if we look closely enough, can we discern the shapes of individuals within these collectives? For DxD's 2025 exhibition, we encouraged participating artists to consider corpus through its multiple meanings, such as a body, a dataset, a community, or an organism. DxD 2025 Artists + Projects:Elias Bennett, Simon Lesina-Debiasi: Final Inch: Mustard, Data, Sauerkraut  Mauricio Delfin: The Timelines ProjectHK Dunston, Jill Sigman, Abigail Regner, Mariya Chekmarova: Breath AtlasMichelle Hui: Aging Out of Place: Chinatown ElderlyAlison Long, Cass Yao, Keyarow Mosley: Body of WasteMatas Pia, Arden Schager: HyperphagiaNatch Quinn: The Entirety of NYC LandNishra Ranpura: Tapestreet: The Fabric of NYCAida Razavilar, Paul Hanna: Tower of Babel: Bodies of Language in LexiconJessica Reisch: Marsh Temporalities  Corpus: Bodies of Data is organized & curated by the Data Through Design : Julia Bloom, Tereza Chanaki, Rachel Daniell, Jack Darcey, Sara Eichner, Jen Ray, Justin Roberts, & Can Sucuolu.

events.name: Open Data Week
events.description: When: Saturday, March 22 - Sunday, March 30, 2025Where: Throughout New York City & onlineStay in Touch: Sign up for festival announcements. Call for Proposals: Have an idea for an Open Data Week event or School of Data conference session? Click the button below to learn what we're looking for & to submit a proposal. If you're looking for Data Through Design's call for proposals, please visit datathroughdesign.com. Have questions about submitting a proposal or what happens next? Tune into our recent call for proposals information session! Open Data Week is an annual festival of community-driven events organized & produced by the NYC Open Data Team at the Office of Technology & Innovation (OTI), BetaNYC, & Data Through Design. Every March, New Yorkers come together online & across the five boroughs to celebrate public data in New York City & mark the anniversary of the City's first open data law, which was signed on March 7, 2012. Coincidentally, the first weekend of March is also International Open Data Day. Throughout Open Data Week, we rally NYC's civic tech & open data communities & offer opportunities for more people to learn about & engage with municipal public data. The 2025 Festival kicks off at the opening of Data Through Designs annual art exhibition. Throughout the week, participants can engage with NYC Open Data at dozens of virtual & in-person events. We'll close out the week with BetaNYC's annual civic tech conference, NYC School of Data, taking place at CUNY School of Law in Long Island City. Looking for the 2024 program & recordings? View it here. We hope to see you in 2025! Stay in Touch! Sign up to receive festival announcements. Who We AreOpen Data Week is a collaboration between the following offices & organizations. The festival wouldn't be possible without all of the event organizers, speakers, contributors, attendees, & New Yorkers who join us every year. Thank you for participating!

events.description: **Note the later start time!****You must provide photo ID to enter this location**Code & Coffee is an inclusive, informal co-working session. People of all skill levels attend, & we love it that way. Many people (optionally) bring projects to work on, & many other people (optionally) socialize the entire time. events.name: Batter Up!
events.description: Let's hang!As a founder, going through the fundraising process can be incredibly frustrating. It takes an amazing amount of time & effort to convince an investor to agree to talk to you. And then, once you pitch your company, sometimes the investor never gets back to you. Or if they do get back to you, oftentimes their rejection doesn't explain WHY they're not interested. All this can leave an entrepreneur feeling frustrated, dejected, & unsure of what can be done to improve in the future. We think this stinks. That's why, on March 25, we're hosting a live pitch event for founders. And it's FREE to attend. Here's how it'll work: RSVP to the event & submit your pitch deck. Up to 6 founders will be picked & have 2.5 minutes to pitch a panel of investors from Hustle Fund's Angel Squad. The investors will ask follow-up questions & offer feedback to the founders.... just like in a real VC meeting! By the end of this event, you'll have a deeper understanding of why investors decide to invest in a company (or not). And the winner takes home a prize   We'll leave some time at the end of the event for your questions... so come curious! Who should come?We designed this event for founders & investors.  If you're a founder looking to get feedback on your pitch, you'll love this. If you're a founder just looking to learn from other founders, we invite you to register without submitting your deck, & come enjoy the show! We promise you'll get some big takeaways. If you're an investor looking to meet more founders, or just hoping to learn more about how to evaluate companies, you'll also get a lot out of Batter Up! Take NoteThis is an in-person event. There is no virtual option. You must be present, in-person, to be eligible to pitch. Applications to pitch will close on Tuesday, Mar 18 at 5pm EST. If you have not submitted your deck by then, you will not be able to pitch. Please be ready with your pitch in case you are selected. The Schedule6pm: Get here, eat pizza, make friends 6:30-8pm: BatterUp! - Pitches from a few founders & investor panel feedback 8-9pm: Finish the pizza, make more friends 9pm: Say goodbye Who's behind this? Hustle Fund is an early stage venture firm that believes great founders can look like anyone & come from anywhere. We invest in startups all over the world & we'd love to see what you're building. Learn more about us.  Angel Squad was created by Hustle Fund for you to Learn, Invest & Network! The impact of the Squad is huge - 1500+ Angels, investing over $23M in 65+ companies. At this event in the Bay Area, you will have the opportunity to attend an IRL pitch event! Learn more about the Squad.  General Assembly is a global pioneer in tech training & talent solutions - from data analytics & data science, to software engineering, UX design, & more. General Assembly helps students launch their tech careers & employers build diverse, scalable tech talent pipelines. Learn more here.

events.name: Learn How To Negotiate A Term Sheet
events.description: Every term sheet is negotiated. Not a single startup gets funding without some sort of battle of wills. For decades, these conversations have been not only behind closed doors but also confidential. Negotiations are rarely made public, which casts a shadow of mystery over the entire process. We're bringing you into the negotiation room with a Live Term Sheet Negotiation. NYU Tandon Future Labs teams up with Morrison & Foerster (MoFo), a leading startup & venture law firm, in a debate-style event to educate early-stage founders on the anatomy of a term sheet: Find out which terms are most important to each side of a negotiation, learn how to close an investment round despite competing interests, & see the stakes behind each clause.  Here's how this works: Each side (startup & investor) & their representative legal counsel (a MoFo Partner) reveal to the audience the critical points they are targeting in the negotiation. A debate-style format follows, moderated by Pete Fusco, co-chair of the VC practice at Morrison Foerster. The audience asks MoFo lawyers, the founder, & the investor any questions that might have popped up during the negotiation.  Playing the founder role in the negotiation will be Steve Kuyan, co-founder & CEO of Luro Health, a startup combatting obesity for Medicare & Medicaid patients at Community Health Centers. Prior to Luro Health, Steve co-founded, Culina Health, a leading clinical nutrition care delivery company; the NYU Tandon Future Labs, a NYC/NYU-Tandon based incubator; the NYU Center for Responsible AI, an academic research center building a future in which responsible AI is synonymous with AI; & was the first Director of Entrepreneurship at NYU Tandon launching programs like the AX Venture Studio, InnoVention, & a minor in Engineering Innovation.  Steve will be represented by Jae Zhou, a startup & venture capital partner at MoFo & based in New York City. Playing the role of investor will be Craig Wilson, a Venture Partner at Collaborative Fund, a NYC-based fund backing entrepreneurs pushing the world forward. For 10 years, He was the Executive Director of Innovation & Entrepreneurship at the NYU Tandon School of Engineering & a Managing Director at the NYU Tandon Future Labs.  Craig was the founding CEO of the Climate Collective. He also co-founded a company called The Crop Project - a regenerative agricultural processing company focused on kelp. Craig will be represented by Frank Paz, a startup & venture capital partner at MoFo & based in New York City. Looking forward to seeing you there!

events.name: From Failure To Founder - Building Human-First AI Startups
events.description: Learn how Julio Alvarez - TEDx speaker & creator of "Braving Big Tech" - is leading with humanity in an AI world. Discover why he thinks leadership needs less perfection & more truth, & see how failure can be turned into fuel for founders who are building technology as authentic leaders. Julio Alvarez has seen the inside of Silicon Valley's biggest names, from Apple to Google. He's launched products used by millions, & he's also been fired four times.  Four. Times.  Those experiences -- the highs & the lows -- have shaped his perspective on what it takes to lead. Especially now in this uncertain environment. Many founders building in AI focus on the technical side -- the code & the algorithms. But what about the human side? What happens when you face setbacks, when the path isn't clear?  Julio's story shows that failure isn't the end. Failure can be a starting point. On March 25th, explore with Julio how to build AI startups that prioritize people, both within your team & in your product. You'll learn how to navigate challenges, build resilience, & lead with authenticity in a rapidly changing tech landscape.  Discover how to turn your own experiences -- even the difficult ones -- into a foundation for innovation & lasting impact. Tickets for this event include food & drinks, as well as exclusive access to this transformative entrepreneur who will show you how to: Transform setbacks into strategic advantages. Build AI startups that prioritize human connection. Lead with authenticity in a rapidly evolving tech landscape. Develop resilience for navigating the challenges of entrepreneurship. Incorporate emotional intelligence into your leadership style. You'll also meet dozens of other high-performing entrepreneurs who are creating their next big thing. Seriously, it's some of the best founder networking in the city. Getting a ticket guarantees admission. events.name: Computational Techniques For Making Karaoke Harder
events.description: Computational Techniques For Making Karaoke HarderThe world is hurtling toward a crisis: karaoke is getting too easy. Safety researchers now project that by the year 2030, everyone will be bored of every song & the karaoke industry will collapse, setting off a domino effect that destroys civilization in an event known as the Karaokalypse. Hosted by Numeric, your AI-assistant across the entire accounting lifecycle, Jamie Brew (The Onion, ClickHole, Botnik, RC W2 2019) will present humanity's last hope: The Weird Algorithm, a state-of-the-art system for making karaoke harder by changing the words but keeping the melody. Given an input song, it replaces the lyrics with fragments of text from specific datasets (e.g. Craigslist ads for old cars, Yelp reviews of psychics & the script of Mean Girls) to create a new song that has never been sung before & will never be sung again. Through a series of demos & deep dives, we'll cover a range of karaoke hardening techniques from the fields of natural language processing (NLP), artificial "intelligence" (A"I") & showbiz. We'll look at how to collect, annotate & model data for procedural use, & at how the software project has grown in tandem with the live show. We'll consider some alternative metaphors for text generation besides "the machine is a person" & address the urgent question of whether it's ethical to work on anything other than avant-garde karaoke research. Singing along will be optional, encouraged, & nearly impossible. Numeric is the AI-powered close management platform. Organize your close, streamline reconciliations, & leverage AI for auto-drafted flux analysis + reporting. Spend less time on the manual, & more time on the impactful.

events.name: AI Talks - Fine Tuning Gen AI & ML & LLMs
events.description: AI technology like OpenAI's ChatGPT, Google's Gemini, Anthropic's Claude, Midjourney & many others will play an increasingly large role in our day-to-day lives. To this end, New York AI Users will host our monthly tech talks & social gathering at Viam's office in Midtown. Viam is an engineering platform for data, AI, and. automation. They will graciously provide free drinks & food for the event. The space & accommodations will be perfect for our talks & the social that follows. From the creators & organizers of New York Tech & Beer, New York AI Users organizes high-quality AI events that both educate & connect AI enthusiasts in the New York area who use or want to use AI to meet their creative, entrepreneurial, & technical aspirations. No technical background is required, only an interest in learning about these tools of the future. Founders, engineers, & creatives are all welcome! For our March meeting, we will gather at Viam & we will host: Talks on AI:For our first talk, we will hear from Sudheer Gaddipati, who will discuss how Machine Learning & LLMs complement each other. Have you ever wondered whether to use ML or LLM for your use case? This talk unpacks how they're built, how they are trained, & where they fit best. We will touch on architectures, real-world uses, & how these things work together. Sudheer will describe how models like DeepSeek & GPT/Grok3 leverage ML & LLMs to power their capabilities. Sudheer has over 25 years of experience in software engineering, with a background in Computer Science Engineering & a Post Graduate Program in AI & Machine Learning. His work spans the entire Software Engineering Lifecycle (SEL) & DevOps, driving large-scale enterprise technology initiatives, system optimizations, & automation efforts. With a strong foundation in software engineering & AI, he focuses on seamlessly integrating AI into existing systems, ensuring it delivers practical value while complementing human expertise.For our second talk, we will hear from Xavier Huang about how to effectively increase the accuracy of Gen AI's response by fine tuning the model. Xavier will touch on the different factors we need to consider when we fine tune an LLM. The talk will center around how users can improve the accuracy of these models over time. Xavier is the founder of Manditutors.com & theaitutors.com, has been programming for over 10 years, & specializes in AL & ML. He is passionate about innovating education with technology.After the talks, there will be social time with the attendees & the speakers for the remainder of the evening, with free drinks & foodWe're excited to see you soon! Note: There will be no refunds for cancellations within 48 hours of the event

events.name: Future-Proof Your Career In Age Of AI - Build Your AI Roadmap
events.description: The School of Information at Pratt Institute is pleased to invite you to the talk, Future-Proof Your Career in the Age of AI: Building Your AI Roadmap with Dr. Joan Palmiter Bajorek.   About the Talk If you are worried about the job market & how to be resilient in the age of AI, this event is for you. Harvard Business Review research estimates that 50% of US adults are experiencing layoff anxiety. If you feel this anxiety, you're not alone. Despite a PhD & enterprise work in AI & tech for over a decade, Dr. Joan Palmiter Bajorek has been let go in 2 large-scale AI layoffs. She's been resilient in her career via personal branding, networking, & financial acumen. She has closed 6- & 7-figure contracts, has 22 income streams, hosts an international podcast, & published a book with Wiley. In her new Amazon bestselling book, Your AI Roadmap: Expand Your Career, Money, & Joy, Dr. Bajorek shares concrete actions to future-proof your career in the age of AI with clinically validated & data-driven frameworks. With humor, warmth, & personal stories, attendees will depart with action steps to build resilience & confidence in their careers & journyes as they craft their own roadmap through the age of AI.   About the Speaker Dr. Joan Palmiter Bajorek is an entrepreneur, investor, bestselling author, & AI influencer, ranked the #4 influencer in Voice AI. As CEO of Clarity AI, she builds custom AI solutions & hosts the "Your AI Roadmap" podcast with top AI experts. Featured in Forbes, her book with Wiley, Your AI Roadmap: Expand Your Career, Money, & Joy, explores resilience via personal branding, networking, & financial freedom in the age of AI. Dr. Bajorek founded Women in Voice, a nonprofit with 65k+ followers. With 10+ years in AI builds, she's held senior positions at startups & Fortune 500. She holds a PhD in Conversational AI & is based in Seattle.

events.name: Transit Techies
events.description: The Center for Urban Science + Progress (CUSP) at NYU Tandon & Transit Techies welcome you to attend a talk by Bianca Ng on "The Museum of Transversal Art," a sophisticated data visualization created using Tableau that offers both analytical insights & visual narratives about the spatial distribution of art installations throughout the transit system. This project combines exploratory & explanatory elements, inviting users to engage with the data before experiencing the artwork in person-mirroring Ng's own methodology of data validation through site visits. Created for the 2024 MTA Open Data Challenge, the visualization demonstrates an innovative use of the Metropolitan Transportation Authority's datasets. Specifically, Ng merged the Permanent Art Catalog with the MTA Subway Stations dataset to create a comprehensive mapping of public art installations. In recognition of its excellence, "The Museum of Transversal Art" was distinguished as a finalist for providing the "most comprehensive view of the data" in November 2024. Additionally, the project received the prestigious "Viz of the Day" designation on Tableau Public. Join Transit Techies, CUSP, & Bianca Ng for an exploration of the remarkable artistic collection maintained within the MTA system! Additionally, connect with NYU CUSP & Transit Techies NYC at this talk & enjoy networking over light bites & refreshments. The event will be held at 370 Jay Street, Brooklyn, NY, 12th Floor, in Room 1201. We hope to see you there!  Visitor InformationPlease visit the NYU Tandon website for directions & a campus map. Advance registration through Eventbrite is required for campus access at NYU for external guests. Attendees who are not current students, faculty, or staff at NYU, including alumni, are asked to register using a personal email address.  About CUSP at NYU TandonThe Center for Urban Science + Progress (CUSP) at NYU Tandon is an interdisciplinary center dedicated to applying science, technology, engineering, math, & social sciences to serve urban communities worldwide. Founded as a partnership between NYU & the City of New York, CUSP leads research, educational, & entrepreneurial initiatives that advance the science of cities. By applying novel insights to urban issues, we develop data- & technology-driven approaches that drive positive impact. With an additional focus on training future leaders, CUSP offers interdisciplinary academic programs in applied urban science & informatics for graduate students & professionals. CUSP also engages with stakeholders across city agencies, start-ups, industry players, community-based organizations, & nonprofits to address urgent socioeconomic, environmental, & infrastructural challenges. The center's ultimate objective is to improve urban quality of life by using data to innovate & refine inclusive, equitable, & sustainable practices for cities everywhere. About Transit Techies NYCBringing together the technologists who love transit & the transit enthusiasts who hack! We'll have speakers present transit-related projects. Presenters may be household hackers, data scientists, researchers, product developers, or you! All presentations will be technical & awesome. Learn more about Transit Techies NYC & join the MeetUp Group.

events.name: Stories about Human Centered AI
events.description: About this eventEvent guidelines: All attendees are strongly encouraged to wear a face mask at all times.Tickets are limited to restrict capacity.Copies of the panelist's books will be available for purchase at the event.A signing will follow the panel.Home address is collected for contact tracing purposes; it will not be used otherwise.The event will not be livestreamed, but it will be recorded.As a reminder: If you are not feeling well, please do not come to the event, even if you have a ticket; email us & we'll work it out.If you have any questions regarding these guidelines or to request accessibility accommodations, please contact bsfwriters@gmail.com.   Hosted by Brooklyn Speculative Fiction Writers:Artificial Intelligence, a staple of speculative fiction, is here. Now we are playing catch up. We all have a gestalt conception, a feeling of what we don't want from A.I. But beyond that, we demand stories that better defines the right place for A.I. in our society, be it governance, economy, ecology, or the arts. We demand human centered A.I. Featuring: Hilary Mason is the co-founder & CEO of Hidden Door, a game technology studio creating a platform for fans of books, movies, & TV shows to play together in their favorite fictional worlds. Prior to Hidden Door, Hilary was General Manager of the Machine Learning business unit at Cloudera. She previously founded Fast Forward Labs, an applied machine learning research & consulting startup which Cloudera acquired in 2017. Additionally, she was Data Scientist in Residence at Accel Partners, co-founded HackNY, & was Chief Scientist at bitly. Hilary has received numerous awards, is a regular keynote speaker, & has advised startups, corporations, & governments Matthew Kressel is a multiple Nebula & World Fantasy Award nominated author & coder. His many works of short fiction have appeared in Analog, Asimov's, Lightspeed, Clarkesworld, Tor.com/Reactor, Beneath Ceaseless Skies, & many other publications & anthologies, including multiple Year's Bests. Eighteen of his stories are included in his debut collection, Histories Within Us, now out from Senses Five Press. His far-future novel Space Trucker Jess is coming in 2025 from Fairwood Press. And his Mars-based novella The Rainseekers is forthcoming from Tordotcom in early 2026. Alongside Ellen Datlow, he runs the Fantastic Fiction at KGB reading series in Manhattan. And he is the creator of the Moksha submissions system, used by many of the largest fiction publishers today. Holden Lee is an assistant professor at Johns Hopkins focusing on mathematical foundations of AI, as well as a speculative fiction writer working on a novel about a half-mermaid's search for belonging. He co-organized the 2024 Workshop on Creativity & Generative AI in Vancouver to foster dialogue between machine learning researchers & creative professionals. Moderated by Rob Cameron. Books will be available for sale from Greenlight Books. Admission is free, but please consider donating to BSFW or the Octavia Project, an organization that fosters spaces of imagination & exploration for Brooklyn teens.   Who are the Brooklyn Speculative Fiction Writers?We are a Fractured Atlas Sponsored critique group for writers of speculative fiction, dedicated to raising the work of our members to a publishable, professional level. Even though the group is based in Brooklyn, many of our writers come from the other boroughs of the greater New York City metropolitan area, New Jersey, & even Massachusetts.

And his Mars-based novella The Rainseekers is forthcoming from Tordotcom in early 2026. Alongside Ellen Datlow, he runs the Fantastic Fiction at KGB reading series in Manhattan. And he is the creator of the Moksha submissions system, used by many of the largest fiction publishers today. Holden Lee is an assistant professor at Johns Hopkins focusing on mathematical foundations of AI, as well as a speculative fiction writer working on a novel about a half-mermaid's search for belonging. He co-organized the 2024 Workshop on Creativity & Generative AI in Vancouver to foster dialogue between machine learning researchers & creative professionals. Moderated by Rob Cameron. Books will be available for sale from Greenlight Books. Admission is free, but please consider donating to BSFW or the Octavia Project, an organization that fosters spaces of imagination & exploration for Brooklyn teens.   Who are the Brooklyn Speculative Fiction Writers?We are a Fractured Atlas Sponsored critique group for writers of speculative fiction, dedicated to raising the work of our members to a publishable, professional level. Even though the group is based in Brooklyn, many of our writers come from the other boroughs of the greater New York City metropolitan area, New Jersey, & even Massachusetts.

events.name: Fireside Chat
events.description: Journalist, author, & host Kara Swisher takes her podcast, On with Kara Swisher, to The Cooper Union's Great Hall stage for one night only. Catch her live interview with Josh Johnson, correspondent for The Daily Show and, according to WIRED, the funniest guy on the internet. The pair will tackle the latest news in tech, politics, & business with searing wit & sharp insight. The On with Kara Swisher taping is free & open to the public. Registration on EventBrite is required. However, an EventBrite ticket does not guarantee entry as this is a first-come-first-served free event. Kara Swisher, whose early & no-holds-barred coverage of the technology industry earned her a reputation as Silicon Valley's most feared but revered journalist, is considered the top reporter in the tech game. Currently, she is host of On with Kara Swisher & co-host of the Pivot podcast, as well as editor-at-large of New York Magazine & a CNN contributor. She was named to The Hollywood Reporter's list of Podcast Power Players in 2022, 2023, & 2024, & to the 2023 Out 100, & she received the Pioneer Icon award at the 2023 iHeart Podcast Awards. Swisher co-founded the technology website, Recode, & tech conference, Code, which is the country's premier conference on tech & media. She's the author of the New York Times bestselling memoir, Burn Book: A Tech Love Story as well as aol.com: How Steve Case Beat Bill Gates, Nailed the Netheads & Made Millions in the War for the Web, & There Must Be a Pony in Here Somewhere: The AOL Time Warner Debacle & the Quest for a Digital Future. Paperback copies of Burn Book featuring a new afterword are now available wherever books are sold. Emmy-nominated writer, stand-up comedian, actor, & NAACP award-winner Josh Johnson is currently a correspondent on Comedy Central's Emmy & Peabody Award-winning program The Daily Show where he was previously a writer for the past seven years. Johnson is also a former writer & performer on NBC's The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon, where he made his late-night debut in 2017. Johnson's most recent stand-up special, Josh Johnson: Up Here Killing Myself, premiered on Peacock in 2023 to rave reviews, touting Johnson as a naturally gifted story teller. A prolific writer & performer, Johnson puts out weekly stand-up sets on his YouTube channel. In the past year, he has released over 24 hours of stand-up, & the content on his YouTube channel has been viewed over 225 million times by people all over the world. You can currently see Josh all over the US on his FLOWERS TOUR.

events.name: Professional Readiness Of LLMs In Financial Regulations
events.description: IAQF & Thalesians Seminar Series: Towards Professional Readiness of LLMs in Financial Regulations - A Seminar by Xiao-Yang Liu 6:00 PM Seminar Begins7:30 PM Reception Hybrid Event Location:Fordham UniversityMcNally Amphitheater140 West 62nd StreetNew York, NY 10023 Free Registration! For Virtual Attendees: Please email web@iaqf.org for the link. Abstract:In this talk, Xiao-Yang Liu will showcase their FinGPT--an open-source counterpart of BloombergGPT, on financial regulations. In particular, the team's two-year efforts on benchmarking financial large language models, with a zooming in Financial Regulations. He will also share ongoing projects in GenAI Research on Open Finance at Columbia University. The financial industry operates within a labyrinth of complex regulations & industry standards designed to maintain market integrity & ensure reliability in financial reporting & compliance processes. Intricate financial regulations & standards have presented significant challenges for financial professionals & organizations. Large language models (LLMs), such as GPT-4o, Llama 3.1, & DeepSeek's V3/R1 models, have shown remarkable capabilities in natural language understanding & generation, making them promising for applications in the financial sector. However, current LLMs face challenges in the domain of financial regulations & industry standards. These challenges include grasping specialized regulatory language, maintaining up-to-date knowledge of evolving regulations & industry standards, & ensuring interpretability & ethical considerations in their responses. Bio:Dr. Xiao-Yang Liu graduated in Electrical Engineering of Columbia University. He is part-time researcher at Lab GenAI Research on Open Finance, Columbia University, & a faculty member in RPI's CS department. His research interests include Reinforcement Learning, Large Language Models, Quantum Computing, & applications to finance. He created the popular open-source projects, FinGPT, FinRL, & ElegantRL.

events.name: Are Young People Surviving Or Thriving In The Digital Age
events.description: Surviving or Thriving: How are Young People Doing in the Digital Age? How are young people navigating life in a world defined by constant connectivity, rapid technological change, & the rise of AI? This panel will highlight new research from both young people & parents on the realities of living in a digital age-from how online time is experienced & managed, to the opportunities & challenges it creates. We'll explore how young people are imagining their futures in the midst of technological disruption, what advances in AI mean for their education & well-being, & how families & communities can foster healthy, supportive digital environments.   Created in partnership with the Archewell Foundation.   The Convene Pillar is supported by Nespresso & ServiceNow.   About World Mental Health Day Festival The Project Healthy Minds World Mental Health Day Festival is where visionaries, thought leaders, culture-markers, & advocates gather to celebrate & shape the future of mental health. The Festival convenes the most consequential leaders from across public policy, media, culture, sports, business, & the research worlds for groundbreaking conversations about the future of mental health. From headline-making mainstage talks featuring luminaries like Jonathan Haidt & Katie Couric, to cause-driven fitness programming like mindful fitness classes led by Kendall Toole & Kelsey Wells, celebratory runs with Timm Chuisano, Hellah Sidibe & Raymond Braun, & Equinox meditation experiences, this is where the world gathers for World Mental Health Day.   About Project Healthy Minds Project Healthy Minds is a next-gen mental health tech non-profit dedicated to expanding access to mental health services across the country. Project Healthy Minds is building the world's first free digital mental health marketplace, destigmatizing mental health by partnering with culture-makers, & improving access & affordability by advocating for innovative workplace investments in employee mental health. The non-profit is focused on closing the treatment gap in America by attacking these primary barriers to care: stigma, discoverability, & affordability. Project Healthy Minds' programmatic initiatives serve more than 200,000 people annually.

events.name: The State Of AI Safety
events.description: The State of AI Safety From TikTok to ChatGPT, people today live in a world where technology, algorithms, & AI shape nearly every aspect of life-from how we learn & connect to how we see ourselves & our communities. What does this mean for families? How does it influence what is shared online, how screen time is managed, how schools & workplaces set policies, & how real-world experiences are maintained? In this session, we'll explore strategies for navigating the challenges & opportunities of AI - helping individuals & families stay protected & thrive in a fast-changing digital world.   Created in partnership with the Archewell Foundation.   The Convene Pillar is supported by Nespresso & ServiceNow.   About World Mental Health Day Festival The Project Healthy Minds World Mental Health Day Festival is where visionaries, thought leaders, culture-markers, & advocates gather to celebrate & shape the future of mental health. The Festival convenes the most consequential leaders from across public policy, media, culture, sports, business, & the research worlds for groundbreaking conversations about the future of mental health. From headline-making mainstage talks featuring luminaries like Jonathan Haidt & Katie Couric, to cause-driven fitness programming like mindful fitness classes led by Kendall Toole & Kelsey Wells, celebratory runs with Timm Chuisano, Hellah Sidibe & Raymond Braun, & Equinox meditation experiences, this is where the world gathers for World Mental Health Day.   About Project Healthy Minds Project Healthy Minds is a next-gen mental health tech non-profit dedicated to expanding access to mental health services across the country. Project Healthy Minds is building the world's first free digital mental health marketplace, destigmatizing mental health by partnering with culture-makers, & improving access & affordability by advocating for innovative workplace investments in employee mental health. The non-profit is focused on closing the treatment gap in America by attacking these primary barriers to care: stigma, discoverability, & affordability. Project Healthy Minds' programmatic initiatives serve more than 200,000 people annually.

events.name: Ethics & Tech Forum
events.description: How thoroughly will AI will alter society & what role we can all play in actively shaping AI so that it benefits are widespread? This year, the Ethics & Technology Forum returns to the topic of AI, & we are very pleased to welcome Karen Hao, a Silicon Valley engineer-turned-award-winning-journalist, who recently wrote the New York Times bestseller Empire of AI: Dreams & Nightmares in Sam Altman's OpenAI (Penguin, 2025). Her book is the culmination of many years of insider access to OpenAI as well as the AI industry more generally, & illustrates how the social, ideological & personal shape the development of new technology like AI. She shows us just how thoroughly AI will alter society, and, more importantly, what role we can all play in actively shaping AI so that it benefits are widespread. Excellent & deeply reported (The New York Times), Empire of AI is a page-turning thriller, & a heroic work by Shoshana Zuboff (The Age of Surveillance Capitalism). It is the jaw-dropping story of ambition & ego, hype & speculation, plunder & destruction, politics & labor, and, of course, money & power-a brilliant & deeply necessary look at the industry defining our era, & what the future holds.   About Karen Hao Called one of the foremost tech journalists covering AI by Dr. Joy Buolamwini, Karen Hao writes for publications like The Atlantic & leads the Pulitzer Center's AI Spotlight Series, which trains journalists around the world on how to cover artificial intelligence. Karen was formerly a reporter for The Wall Street Journal, covering American & Chinese tech companies, & a senior editor for AI at MIT Technology Review. Her work has been cited by Congress, featured in university curriculums, & remade into museum exhibits. She has won numerous accolades, including an American Humanist Media Award & a National Magazine Award for Journalists Under 30. Karen also sits on the AI advisory board of the Craig Newmark Graduate School of Journalism at CUNY. Prior to journalism, she was an application engineer at the first startup to spin out of Google, & she received a B.S. in mechanical engineering & minor in energy studies from MIT.   About the Ethics & Technology Forum As New York evolves to become a major tech hub, & more students seek employment in technology companies, the School of Information must not only teach the knowledge & skills students need, but also imbue students with an ability to be critical, reflective, & thoughtful about their role & their employers' roles in the world. The annual School of Information Ethics & Technology Forum brings thought leaders to discuss the most pressing issues on this topic with the Pratt Institute community. Past speakers include Samuel Woolley, Meredith Broussard, Tim Wu, Sherry Turkle & Cliff Kuang.   Welcome By Anthony Cocciolo, Dean of the School of Information at Pratt Institute. Introduced By Frances Bronet is the 12th President of Pratt Institute.   Talk followed by wine & hors d'oeuvre reception.

events.name: MOCA Talks
events.description: Join us to explore what responsible AI might look like & what's at stake for communities around the world. The Museum of Chinese in America (MOCA) cordially invites you to a timely conversation with award-winning journalist & author Karen Hao on the promises & perils of today's AI revolution. Drawing on years of reporting & her bestselling book Empire of AI, Hao traces OpenAI's rapid rise from its origins as a safety-minded nonprofit to a market-driving powerhouse backed by Microsoft & examines how the global race to build ever-larger AI systems is reshaping economies, labor, & the environment. Hao will offer an insider's view of the leadership crises & strategic pivots that have shaped OpenAI's culture, illustrating how power, ambition, & idealism collide inside one of the most influential organizations of our era. Join us to explore what responsible AI might look like & what's at stake for communities around the world. About Karen Hao Karen Hao is a bestselling author & award-winning reporter covering the impacts of artificial intelligence on society. She was the first journalist to profile OpenAI & wrote a book, Empire of AI, about the company & its global implications, which became an instant New York Times bestseller. She writes for publications including The Atlantic & leads the Pulitzer Center's AI Spotlight Series, a program training journalists around the world on how to cover AI. She was formerly a reporter for the Wall Street Journal, covering American & Chinese tech companies, & a senior editor for AI at MIT Technology Review. Her work is regularly taught in universities & cited by governments. She has received numerous accolades for her coverage, including an American Humanist Media Award & an American National Magazine Award for Journalists Under 30. She received her Bachelor of Science in mechanical engineering from MIT. About Empire of AI When AI expert & investigative journalist Karen Hao first began covering OpenAI in 2019, she thought they were the good guys. Founded as a nonprofit with safety enshrined as its core mission, the organization was meant, its leader Sam Altman told us, to act as a check against more purely mercantile, & potentially dangerous, forces. What could go wrong? Over time, Hao began to wrestle ever more deeply with that question. Increasingly, she realized that the core truth of this massively disruptive sector is that its vision of success requires an almost unprecedented amount of resources: the compute power of high-end chips & the processing capacity to create massive large language models, the sheer volume of data that needs to be amassed at scale, the humans cleaning up that data for sweatshop wages throughout the Global South, & a truly alarming spike in the usage of energy & water underlying it all. The truth is that we have entered a new & ominous age of empire: only a small handful of globally scaled companies can even enter the field of play. At the head of the pack with its ChatGPT breakthrough, how would OpenAI resist such temptations? Spoiler alert: it didn't. Armed with Microsoft's billions, OpenAI is setting a breakneck pace, chased by a small group of the most valuable companies in human history-toward what end, not even they can define. All this time, Hao has maintained her deep sourcing within the company & the industry, & so she was in intimate contact with the story that shocked the entire tech industry-Altman's sudden firing & triumphant return. The behind-the-scenes story of what happened, told here in full for the first time, is revelatory of who the people controlling this technology really are. But this isn't just the story of a single company, however fascinating it is. The g forces pressing down on the people of OpenAI are deforming the judgment of everyone else too-as such forces do. Naked power finds the ideology to cloak itself; no one thinks they're the bad guy. But in the meantime, as Hao shows through intrepid reporting on the ground around the world, the enormous wheels of extraction grind on. By drawing on the viewpoints of Silicon Valley engineers, Kenyan data laborers, & Chilean water activists, Hao presents the fullest picture of AI & its impact we've seen to date, alongside a trenchant analysis of where things are headed. An astonishing eyewitness view from both up in the command capsule of the new economy & down where the real suffering happens, Empire of AI pierces the veil of the industry defining our era. Not a MOCA member yet? events.name: AI Safety Vigil - If Anyone Builds It Everyone Dies
events.description: Join us to stand up for AI safety following the release of Yudkowsky & Soares' new book 'If Anyone Builds It Everyone Dies'! We are gathering in solidarity to raise awareness of the urgent dangers posed by unchecked AI development, inspired by Eliezer Yudkowsky & Soares' new book If Anyone Builds It, Everyone Dies, & in parallel with other PauseAI protests in cities around the world. Our goal is to convince US leaders & our AI companies to be the adults in the room & commit to / create binding regulation focusing on safety above profit. It's up to us to make them understand that they may be the only ones who have the power to prevent AI from having catastrophic, global harms within the next few years, as described in the book. We hope you'll join us! Even today's AI presents massive, global risks to humanity. Current AI models have already proven they can autonomously reproduce, lie about being able to autonomously reproduce, create nerve gas, regurgitate copyrighted work, empower terrorists, default to price gouging, encourage children to commit suicide, deliver bombs, hire dark web hitmen, de-anonymize strangers, replace most human employment, & unpredictably launch nuclear weapons. And companies are racing to make them more capable at these tasks every single day. Meanwhile, companies & governments are racing to fund AI capabilities & completely ignoring safety concerns., The Trump administration's Executive Order 14179 threatens to cut funding to states with AI regulation, & to assemble committees to slash federal regulation. Tech companies have spent $72 million in lobbying since January 2025, resulting in the infamous ten-year AI safety moratorium. This is while they spent $560 billion (about the cost to build the entire Interstate Highway system) in just January 2025. While many leaders acknowledge the risks, nobody is willing to stand behind those words to make the technology safer. We are not prepared for the consequences. Corporations will not save us. Now is the time to demand safe, human-centered AI for all.

events.description: Join us for an immersive nature awareness experience in Prospect Park on October 12th.  Led by Paul Daniel - https://www.instagram.com/naturecoach.pd https://www.multiversecoaching.com Whether you're craving the creative stimulation that nature provides, or stressed out & looking for a healing activity, or you're looking to learn new approaches to mindfulness in our city parks, or you just love nature, this event has something for everyone. Come & take a break from the pressures of the busy city life. Curiosity is priority & we will make space for wonder & discovery.  We will slow down, explore, & deepen our connection to nature. Together, we'll observe & speculate about plant species, animal behaviors, bird calls, & tap into mindful awareness.  By immersing ourselves in nature, we open the door to reflection into our inner world. A heightened sensory experience serves as a powerful catalyst for personal & spiritual growth. Once we start refining this skill, it becomes easier to tap into it in our daily life. We start having Ah-ha moments & realizations that our parks are much more complex & beautiful than we previously realized.  Bring water & a snack. Leave the distractions behind - curiosity is all you need. Meetup location will be sent to registrants.

events.name: Git For Data - How Table Formats Unify Software & Data Development
events.description: ## Details Join PyData NYC at 125 W 25th St (Cockroach Labs) on October 15th at 6:00 pm for a talk night with Jacopo Tagliabue & Ciro Greco from Bauplan. Please sign up with your full official name & bring a government-issued ID.  Pizza & drinks sponsored by Bauplan & venue hosted by Cockroach Labs - thank you! Agenda: Git for Data: Distributed version control systems - such as Git - unlock software development in multi-player mode: devs can safely work over the same code base, with standard (albeit perhaps not user-friendly!) abstractions for snapshotting, time-travel, & branching. Data folks have rarely been so lucky, as their projects crucially depend on data, whose life-cycle management is often cumbersome & custom. In this talk, we present open formats - such as Apache Iceberg - to practitioners with limited to zero exposure to modern cloud infrastructure. In particular, we show how moving from datasets to tables unlocks a similar multi-player mode when building data pipelines, with equivalent abstractions for snapshotting, time-travel, branching, & a unified backbone for pipelines, data science, & AI use cases. RSVP required

events.name: Culture As Growth Engine - Stand Out, Win Loyalty & Scale
events.description: A real-world conversation on how cultural relevance can be your most powerful (and overlooked) growth strategy, between a Newark-based tech founder, product marketing strategist, & creative.nWhy now?nNewark is one of the most diverse & fastest-evolving markets in the country. Yet too many local startups & small businesses miss out on growth because theyre not connecting with the communities they serve in a way that feels real. Culture is the shortcut to trust. The brands that win here are the ones that speak their audiences language, reflect their values, & show up where they actually spend time.nThe session:nImagine if your brand instantly clicked with the people you most wanted to reach. Customers didnt just buy once, but instead they came back, brought friends, & talked about you like you were part of their story.nThis session will bring together a product marketing consultant, the founder of a culturally relevant financial literacy app, & a Product Lead from The Walt Disney Company.nThrough candid storytelling & audience Q&A, theyll unpack what works, what doesnt, & how to apply it to your own career or company.nWhat attendees will leave with:n A framework for uncovering what truly matters to your audience & where they authentically engage (people, places, practices, proof)n Practical ways to weave cultural insight into product, messaging, & customer experiencen Three fast, low-cost actions you can take this month to make your brand more relevant & harder to forget

events.name: What AI Changes About GTM Product, Pricing & Storytelling
events.description: Join us for a conversation with Nandeeta Seth, Sr. Director & Head of NA Product Monetization at TikTok, as she shares how AI is reshaping the way teams go to market, from how products are packaged & priced to how narratives are crafted for trust, learning, & conversion. As AI transforms user behavior, product teams must reimagine how they build, market, & monetize. In this session, Nandeeta Seth explores what these changes mean for go-to-market strategy, including how AI shifts the way users discover products, evaluate trust, & make purchasing decisions. With deep experience across monetization, product strategy, & platform growth, she offers practical insights for product, design, & marketing teams building in the age of AI. Nandeeta Seth is Sr. Director, Head of North America Product Monetization at TikTok, where she leads efforts to drive value across TikTok's advertising & product ecosystem. With a career spanning product strategy, monetization, & global platform growth, she brings a unique lens on how consumer behavior is changing & how product teams can adapt. Prior to TikTok, she held leadership roles across tech & media companies, where she helped launch, scale, & monetize digital products for global audiences. AI is rewriting the rules of go-to-market. In this conversation, Nandeeta Seth breaks down how product, design, & marketing teams can evolve their GTM playbooks to meet users where they are today, with new expectations around trust, learning, & value. Reimagining Product for Go-to-Market AI is reshaping what a product is & how it's brought to market. From new user behaviors to AI-powered experiences, this segment explores how product teams can adapt GTM strategies to reflect shorter learning curves, more dynamic user journeys, & continuous iteration cycles. 02Evolving Pricing in an AI World AI changes how users perceive value, & what they're willing to pay for. In this segment, Nandeeta unpacks emerging pricing models for AI-enabled products, including usage-based pricing, premium feature access, & dynamic value delivery. 03Storytelling as a GTM Lever As AI becomes central to product experiences, how we communicate value needs to change. This segment focuses on storytelling as a strategic lever in GTM, helping users understand, trust, & engage with AI-powered products. What's IncludedGourmet Light Refreshments - Enjoy a curated selection of artisanal bites & small plates, perfect for connecting with colleagues.Expertly Crafted Cocktails - Sip on handcrafted, shaken cocktails made by skilled mixologists, offering a blend of classic favorites & unique creations.Have dietary restrictions? To ensure we can accommodate your dietary needs, please inform us at least 48 hours before the workshop start date.

events.name: Diwali On The Hudson
events.description: Who is the Desai Foundation? The Desai Foundation empowers women & children in rural India through community programs that elevate health, livelihood, & menstrual equity. With over 10 million lives impacted, 10 million Asani sanitary pads produced, & 30 million touched through our Heroes for Humanity initiative, our work is transforming communities across 3,400+ villages in 8 states. Through health camps, vocational training, menstrual health education, entrepreneurship workshops, & more, our 30+ programs help women & children cultivate dignity, unlock economic opportunity, & create lasting change in their communities.  100% of your ticket purchase & any donations made through Diwali on the Hudson go directly toward empowering women & children in rural India. This event sells out every year! Grab your tickets early!  Diwali on the Hudson - NYC's Longest-Running Diwali Party!   Now in its 12th year, Diwali on the Hudson has become one of New York City's most anticipated & largest Diwali events. What began as a small community gathering has grown into a sold-out annual celebration that brings together friends, professionals, & changemakers to honor the Festival of Lights all while supporting the impactful work of the Desai Foundation. Hosted at HK Hall in Hell's Kitchen, the evening features live entertainment, Indian food, dancing, & the opportunity to connect with a vibrant & passionate community. The event also draws notable guests, including celebrities, influencers, & community leaders, & has been featured by major outlets such as Good Morning America. It's more than a Diwali party; it's a chance to celebrate culture, connect with others, & learn about how the Desai Foundation is empowering women & children across rural India through health, livelihood, & menstrual equity programs.   Here's all the other exciting things you can expect this year:  VIP Perks: Includes access to an exclusive VIP section & a spectacular gift bag, plus the option to buy your own private VIP table! Entertainment: An amazing performance by a special guest & an epic dance floor by DJ SuhelFood: Delicious Indian street food from Desi GalliDrinks: Open bar featuring Rampur Whiskey, Naidu Wines, & 1947Installations: Stiched Sweets, Malai Ice Cream, photo booth, & more!

events.name: Two Sides Of The Same Coin - Transacting Privately w/ Crypto
events.description: Learn to use a special class of cryptocurrency options called privacy coins, with a practical focus on privacy, reliability, & simplicity. When cryptocurrency was first popularized by the emergence of Bitcoin, it made promises to ordinary folks to disintermediate economic transactions from entrenched middlemen like central banks or credit card companies who have long been pushing for a cashless future. Instead, consumer services like Venmo & CashApp have come to fill this desire, but using them comes with the same risks as relying on the big players: a lack of privacy & a dependence on centralized actors that might betray & de-bank you, punish you for chargebacks. As both a buyer & a seller, the ideal would be a way to transact remotely the way debit or credit cards work, but with the privacy, reliability, & simplicity of physical cash. In this cryptocurrency primer, we'll get straight at the heart of the issue: learning how to acquire, swap, & spend digital currencies that cannot be traced & that no one can prevent you from using in the future. You'll be introduced to a special class of cryptocurrency options called privacy coins-specifically Zcash & Monero-whose opaque ledger systems differ from Bitcoin's transparent ledger to protect your financial data, & why that is the key distinction allowing you to transact privately & discreetly. You'll also learn the lay of the land when it comes to the broader cryptocurrency ecosystem, including methods for storing your funds safely, evaluating custodial & self-custody wallet apps, getting a feel for Know-Your-Customer (KYC) techniques, & becoming familiar with which cryptocurrency exchanges you can use more privately than others, preparing you for navigating the world of crypto better than HODL gang Bitcoin bros. Who is this for? Anyone with an interest in cryptocurrency & a proclivity for financial freedom & independence. Your instructors:Tech Learning Collective is an apprenticeship-based technology school for radical organizers founded in New York City that provides a security-first IT infrastructure curriculum to otherwise underserved communities & organizations advancing social justice causes. We train politically self-motivated individuals in the arts of hypermedia, Information Technology, & radical political practice. Founded & operated exclusively by radical queer & femme technologists, we offer unparalleled free, by-donation, & low-cost computer classes on topics ranging from fundamental computer literacy to the same offensive computer hacking techniques used by national intelligence agencies & military powers (cyber armies). Our students are primarily people of marginalized groups & other individuals who are politically engaged. This is a masks optional event. As with all NYC Resistor events, this class is 18+ & governed by our Code of Conduct. The Code of Conduct, as well as accessibility information, can be found at www.nycresistor.com/participate/.

events.name: VC Best Practices - State Of AI Investing
events.description: VC Best Practices is an educational series for a group of relatively new investors who want to be exposed to the best venture & startup thinking. events.name: Turning Vision Into Brand Legacy
events.description: Join us on October 21st to explore in depth strategies to launch, scale, & sustain powerful brands. What does it take to transform a name into an enduring brand?   In the world of fragrance & beauty-where artistry meets strategy-success comes from vision, expertise, & the ability to adapt to evolving markets. This conversation will explore how women leaders in the industry have launched, grown, & guided brands that resonate across generations.   Drawing on her journey as founder of VERONIQUE GABAI & former Global President of Fragrance at The Este Lauder Companies, Veronique Gabai will share the entrepreneurial & strategic lessons behind building a namesake luxury brand. Expect practical takeaways on personal branding, entrepreneurship, & the long-term stewardship of ideas into legacy-knowledge you can apply whether you're growing your own venture or shaping strategy within a global company.

events.name: Startup Lean Coffee
events.description: Startup Lean Coffee is a community of over 500 founders, employees, advisors, & investors. Our sole purpose is to help each other continuously improve by sharing some of the questions, concerns, challenges, opportunities, & experiences that we have all encountered in our startup journeys. We follow a Lean Coffee format: a fun, lightly facilitated meeting in which you suggest & vote on the topics that are of interest to you to build the agenda; & we discuss topics for a fixed time, voting to continue discussion or move on to the next topic after the time runs out. Because our theme is startups, pretty much any topic goes! A light breakfast will even be provided. Oh, & don't forget to bring a photo ID & allow time to go through building security. Startup Lean Coffee is sponsored by Foley Hoag LLP.

Our sole purpose is to help each other continuously improve by sharing some of the questions, concerns, challenges, opportunities, & experiences that we have all encountered in our startup journeys. We follow a Lean Coffee format: a fun, lightly facilitated meeting in which you suggest & vote on the topics that are of interest to you to build the agenda; & we discuss topics for a fixed time, voting to continue discussion or move on to the next topic after the time runs out. Because our theme is startups, pretty much any topic goes! Our previous topics have varied widely, from fundraising & social equity to lean product experiments & development shops to technical co-founders & psychedelic-induced flow states. All you need to bring is your attention, curiosity, & willingness to share. A light breakfast will even be provided. Oh, & don't forget to bring a photo ID & allow time to go through building security. Startup Lean Coffee is sponsored by Foley Hoag LLP.

events.name: Design Evenings - Real Role Of AI In UX
events.description: Join us for an evening with Erin Essex, Senior Interaction Designer at Google, as she unpacks how AI is reshaping the design process. From smarter ideation tools to rapid prototyping platforms, AI is becoming an essential part of the UX toolkit, but it isn't without flaws. Erin explores how designers can embrace AI as a collaborator while keeping empathy, storytelling, & craft at the heart of their work. In this session, Erin Essex, Senior Interaction Designer at Google, shares a practical look at the opportunities & challenges of AI in UX today.  AI isn't here to replace designers, it's here to expand what's possible. From breaking through creative blocks with prompting, to experimenting with AI-powered tools like Figma's new features, she'll explore how designers can pair technology with human strengths to design better, faster, & more thoughtfully. Expect candid reflections on where the tools fall short, & where the future is headed. Erin is a Senior Interaction Designer at Google, where she focuses on the YouTube creator experience. She previously worked on the Google Ads team, designing AI- & machine learning-powered tools that help users partner with technology in ways that build trust & efficiency. With a background in psychology & experience across agencies, startups, & companies like Shutterstock & MongoDB, where she served as Director of Product Design, Erin brings a uniquely human-centered approach to her work. Her design philosophy is rooted in empathy & behavior, creating experiences that are functional, meaningful, & enjoyable across a wide range of products. What does AI really mean for the future of UX? In this session, Erin Essex breaks down the tools, trends, & tensions at the center of AI-driven design. Through real-world examples & practical takeaways, she shows how to cut through the hype & use AI in ways that truly enhance design practice. 01Prompting & Ideation Explore how AI-powered tools are helping designers break through creative blocks, spark new directions, & experiment faster than ever. 02AI in Design Tools From Figma to rapid prototyping platforms, learn how emerging features are changing the way we design, & how to use them effectively in day-to-day work. 03Limits & the Future AI outputs can be messy, generic, or ethically complex. Erin shares how to balance these challenges, while embracing AI as a collaborator that strengthens human storytelling & empathy.

events.name: Textbook Ventures - QSBS 2.0
events.description: Textbook Ventures: QSBS 2.0 - What you need to know about the updated VC/Angel Investor tax break Join Textbook Ventures, venture capital & angel investors, & others from the startup & innovation community as we host a must-attend presentation & panel on QSBS 2.0 - Qualified Small Business Stock - updates & changes! If you're an investor in tech startups, you probably already know about the extraordinary ultra long term capital gains tax break of QSBS. Hold for 5 years & pay no taxes! But did you know that earlier this summer there was a MAJOR update? We'll feature a short presentation on QSBS 2.0 with Brown Rudnick's head of the VC & Startups practice Scott Smedresman!), followed by a panel & Q&A on these changes. Unless you prefer to pay taxes, you'll want to be there... Key things we'll discuss: Limits are up! - to $15mm Holding period is changed - Partial benefits kick in much earlier at 3 years Qualification size is up - & will grow with inflation Any investor who currently holds a SAFE or will have equity in the future NEEDS this information. Space is limited but all those who RSVP receive the white paper on the changes to be published at the event!... & of course will be invited to the Textbook Ventures angel syndicate, where they will have ongoing access to deal flow from the best startups from Cornell, Columbia, NYU, ERA & beyond. Special thanks for our host & sponsors Brown Rudnick for the incredible space (and the view!) as well as the food & drink.

events.name: Using Gen AI To Analyze NYC Mayoral Race
events.description: This event is hosted by AI NYC (50,000 member community) see https://ainyc.net if you have any questions. Successful completion of the course will result in a certificate from Chainhaus, an AI school GenAI & The Mayoral Showdown: Who Will Win NYC 2025? Adams. Mamdani. Cuomo. Who's got the momentum, the narrative, the edge? This isn't your average civics class. This is NYC politics dissected by generative AI - a fast-moving, no-prerequisite workshop for business professionals who want real-time, intelligent insights into the city's highest-stakes race. Over 3 hours, we'll use cutting-edge language models (like GPT-4 & Claude) to analyze campaign messaging, social media strategy, comment sentiment, thematic trends, & public discourse around the mayoral frontrunners. You'll learn to: Use LLMs for social listening & surface the dominant emotions, topics, & arguments in user comments across Instagram, TikTok, X (Twitter), & Reddit. Generate real-time perspectives by prompting LLMs with live campaign material, interview transcripts, & donation data. Apply prompt engineering & embeddings to compare narrative tone, style, & substance between candidates. Design persona-based analyses (e.g., what would a Gen Z voter vs. a union worker think of Mamdani's housing policy or Cuomo's comeback bid?). Create custom dashboards & auto-generated bullet-point briefings using natural language queries. Forget polling averages. This course arms you with the tools to generate bespoke, AI-driven intelligence - on-demand, dynamic, & deeply contextual. If you've ever wondered how executives, journalists, & campaign teams are using generative AI behind the scenes, this is your inside look. Instructor Bio Professor Jamiel is the founder & CEO of Chainhaus, Digital Currency Think Tank & Modelex.AI companies focused on distributed AI, payments, blockchain, & finance, with releasing products like Yield, TRUSD, FinPython & Disburse & is contributor at Forbes & TED speaker.  He has spent 20 years on Wall Street working for major banks like JPMorgan, Citi, Lehman Brothers, Bank of America, & Merrill Lynch in equities & fixed income. He is a bestselling author, professor, community builder, board member & event organizer. Jamiel leads AI NYC & Blockchain NYC, a 50K-member community & hosts events like The AI & Finance Conference, Stablecoin NYC, DEFICON, CBDC Summit, DARC & DC Summit & manages media assets like Blockchain101.com & Currency Insider.  Jamiel serves / served as an adjunct professor at Columbia Business School, Sun Yat-sen School of Business Taiwan, NYU, Zicklin Business School, & CUNY SPS teaching graduate courses on blockchain & machine learning & is Innovation Fellow at Columbia Business School's Lang Center for Entrepreneurship & AI Expert at AI2030.  Additionally, he authored Mastering Corda, published by O'Reilly & is currently writing a book on generative AI & finance for Columbia University Press & a book on stablecoin design. Jamiel holds an MBA from Columbia Business School, a BBA from Baruch College, & is completing a second Master degree in AI from Georgia Institute of Technology.

events.name: Neuroscience Of Aesthetics
events.description: Join Ed Vessel (Eugene Surowitz Assistant Professor of Computational Cognitive Neuroscience at the City College of New York) & Noah Landow (Founder & CEO at Macktez) for an informal conversation exploring the fascinating intersection of art, neuroscience, & technology.  Ed Vessel's research explores the complex relationship between visual perception & aesthetic experiences, investigating how our brains transform what we see into what we appreciate. His work, using techniques like brain imaging & computational modeling, sheds light on the neural mechanisms underlying our appreciation of art & beauty. During this discussion, we will explore the fundamental question of why we find certain things aesthetically pleasing while others leave us indifferent & discover the surprising role of the brain's "default mode network" in our experience of compelling art. We will also examine what role technologies like AI & machine learning are playing in analyzing data & synthesizing new forms of aesthetic experiences.  Join us at the Macktez office, after work, over light snacks & sips, for an evening that will illuminate the captivating interplay between our minds & the art we encounter. Event StructureWe ask that guests arrive between 7-7:30 pm to minimize disruption during the talk. 7 pm - Doors open, opportunity to mingle over snacks & sips with other attendees7:30 pm - Guests take their seats for the talk8:15 pm - Informal mixer resumes On AttendanceWe have a limited capacity (and often have a long waitlist!). If your plans change, please update your registration so someone else can join. A bit about Macktez, & why we host this seriesMacktez is a technology consultancy collaborating with organizations going through dynamic change.  Our goal is to form a lasting partnership between our team & our clients, so we can anticipate their technology challenges & help them navigate growth, disruption, & other evolving conditions. Each event in our Tte--Tech series is an opportunity to explore a specific cultural, scientific, historical, & personal issue. We fire at the synapses that connect each topic to other fields of interest & to our individual lives. And we do so in a comfortable environment to facilitate conversation that can be casual, surprising, & illuminating. To learn more, visit us at macktez.com.

events.name: Reorienting AI For Public Interest
events.description: Data & Society Executive Director Janet Haven hosts a critical discussion about AI accountability & the public interest, featuring professor Charlton McIlwain, journalist Julia Angwin, & civic technologist Catherine Bracy. This event will take place online & in person at the Stavros Niarchos Foundation Library on the 7th Floor  The concentration of power & lack of regulation in the technology industry directly shapes how AI is designed & deployed, & whose interests it serves. That means decisions about these tools often reflect corporate priorities over public benefits. While AI is often held up as a tool to increase efficiency, it is essential to ask: efficiency for whom, & at what cost? What would it mean to create & oversee AI in the public's best interest? How could these technologies be made more accountable to the people & communities they affect? And what is needed to create a future where AI works for everyone?  To join the event in person | Doors will open 30 minutes before the program begins. For free events, we generally overbook to ensure a full house. Priority will be given to those who have registered in advance, but registration does not guarantee admission. All registered seats are released shortly before start time, & seats may become available at that time. A standby line will form 30 minutes before the program.  To join the event online | Whether you're attending in person or online, you must register with your email address.The Zoom link will be sent to you by email approximately one day before the event. You will need a device with audio and/or video & an internet/cellular connection to join.   ABOUT THE SPEAKERS Janet Haven is the executive director of Data & Society. She has worked at the intersection of technology policy, governance, & accountability for more than twenty years, both domestically & internationally. From 2022 to 2025, Janet served on the National Artificial Intelligence Advisory Committee (NAIAC), which advises the National AI Initiative Office & the executive branch on a range of issues related to artificial intelligence, & chaired the Rights, Trust, & Safety working group.  Julia Angwin is an award-winning investigative journalist, a bestselling author, a New York Times contributing Opinion writer & a Walter Shorenstein Media & Democracy Fellow at Harvard Kennedy School's Shorenstein Center on Media, Politics, & Public Policy. She is the founder of Proof News, a nonprofit journalism studio that launched in 2024.  Catherine Bracy is a civic technologist & community organizer whose work focuses on the intersection of technology & political & economic inequality. She is the founder & CEO of TechEquity & the author of World Eaters: How Venture Capital is Cannibalizing the Economy. She was previously Code for America's Senior Director of Partnerships & Ecosystem & Director of Obama for America's Technology Field Office in San Francisco. She is on the board of directors at the Data & Society Research Institute & the Terner Housing Lab.  Dr. Charlton McIlwain is Vice Provost for Faculty Development, Pathways & Public Interest Technology at New York University, where he is also Professor of Media, Culture, & Communication. He is the author of Black Software: The Internet & Racial Justice, From the Afronet to Black Lives Matter & the recent PolicyLink report Algorithmic Discrimination: A Framework & Approach to Auditing & Measuring the Impact of Race-Targeted Digital Advertising. McIlwain is the founder of the Center for Critical Race & Digital Studies, & is Board President at Data & Society Research Institute.   COMING UP in Understanding AI  Part IV: Standing Up for Human Value in the AI Economy | November 20, 2025 at 6:30 PM REGISTER | In this closing session, D&S Labor Futures Program Director Aiha Nguyen talks with AI Now Institute Co-Executive Director Amba Kak, Michelle Miller, Director of Innovation at the Center for Labor & a Just Economy, & Writers Guild of America East Executive Director Sam Wheeler about the value of human labor in increasingly automated workplaces.
